summary: Objects a later migration creates were not all locked down: a new function was executable by anon and authenticated (Postgres's built-in PUBLIC default can't be removed by a per-schema default), the default for new sequences was never revoked, and nothing checked that every table keeps RLS on with no policies.
fix: A migration revokes the defaults for later sequences (anon, authenticated) and later functions (PUBLIC, globally for the migration role); an integration test checks every public table has RLS on and no policy, the two roles hold no privilege on any table, sequence or function, and objects created later get none.
